intro: Arkansas Legislative Audit examines every county and publishes what it finds. This page quotes what the auditors reported about Izard County, from its latest report — no verdict added in either direction. What the auditors said is the record; what to make of it is yours.
regulatory_basis_note: Read this before reading any Arkansas audit: county and city reports carry a technical 'adverse opinion' on GAAP grounds because Arkansas law has them keep books on a simpler 'regulatory basis.' That phrase appears in every such audit in the state and signals the accounting format — not wrongdoing. A report is 'clean' or not in its findings, deficiencies, and noncompliance sections, which is what this page quotes.

verdicts.quote: The result of our tests disclosed instances of noncompliance or other matters that are required to be reported under Government Auditing Standards and which are described in the Report on Internal Control over Financial Reporting section as item 2024-1.
verdicts.detail: On internal control, the auditors wrote: “We identified a certain deficiency in internal control, described below as item 2024-1, that we consider to be a material weakness.”

limits: From the 2024 report, dated October 7, 2025. Read by machine from the report’s text; the quotes are the auditors’ words. Older reports, and the separate federal (single) audits, aren’t on this page yet.
Arkansas alternates between full audits and limited “financial and compliance” reviews; each line says which this is.
